solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{(1+\sin x)(-\sin x)-\cos x(\cos x)}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\&=\frac{-\sin x-\sin^2x-\cos^2x}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\&=\frac{-(1+\sin x)}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\&=\frac{-1}{1+\sin x}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}&=-(-(1+\sin x)^{-2})\cdot(\cos x)\\&=\frac{\cos x}{(1+\sin x)^2}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+y\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{\cos x}{(1+\sin x)^2}+\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\cdot\frac{-1}{1+\sin x}\\&=\frac{\cos x-\cos x}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\&=0\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct first derivative (quotient rule); 1: correct second derivative; 1: substitution showing the result

solutions.latex:
Maximum price will occur when $\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{183}\right)=1$

$$\begin{aligned}\therefore\ P&=180+44\\&=224\text{ cents/litre}\end{aligned}$$

Minimum when $\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{183}\right)=-1$

$$\begin{aligned}\text{i.e. }P&=180-44\\&=136\text{ cents/litre}\end{aligned}$$

Period: $$\begin{aligned}T&=\frac{2\pi}{\frac{2\pi}{183}}\\&=183\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore\ 0\le t\le366\Rightarrow$ two cycles of graph

At $t=0$, $P=180$

\exfigure{165_q12_s1}

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}202&=180+44\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{183}\right)\\22&=44\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{183}\right)\\\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{183}\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\\\frac{2\pi t}{183}&=\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{5\pi}{6},\ \ldots\\t&=\frac{183}{12}\\&=\frac{61}{4}\end{aligned}$$

Petrol first costs 202 c/L when $t=\dfrac{61}{4}$ days (15.25 days)

For $0\le t\le1$, the particle's displacement increases linearly (at 5 m/s)

$$\begin{aligned}x(1)&=6\sqrt{1}-\frac{1}{1}\\&=5\end{aligned}$$

$$x'(t)=3t^{-\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{1}{t^2}$$

For $t>1$, $x'(t)>0\Rightarrow x(t)$ is an increasing function.

$\therefore$ displacement is increasing for $t>0$

$\therefore$ never comes to rest.

OR: as $t\to\infty$, $x'(t)\to0^+$ asymptote $\therefore$ never 0.

solutions.latex:
For intersection

$$\begin{aligned}2\cos x&=\cot x\\2\cos x&=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\\2\sin x\cos x&=\cos x\\2\sin x\cos x-\cos x&=0\\\cos x(2\sin x-1)&=0\qquad0\le x\le2\pi\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore\ \cos x=0\qquad\qquad2\sin x-1=0$

$x=\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\qquad\qquad\sin x=\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\ \ x=\dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$

$$\therefore\ x=\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{6},\ \frac{3\pi}{2}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}\ln(\sin x)&=\frac{1}{\sin x}\times\cos x\\&=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\\&=\cot x\end{aligned}$$

solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct integral expression; 1: correct primitive; 1: correct answer in simplest form

solutions.latex:
For instantaneous rate, need $\dfrac{dT}{dt}$.

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{dt}&=-150\times0.2\ln(0.9)(0.9)^{0.2t}\\&=-30\ln(0.9)(0.9)^{0.2t}\end{aligned}$$

Require $\dfrac{dT}{dt}<1$

$$\begin{aligned}\therefore\ -30\ln(0.9)(0.9)^{0.2t}&<1\\(0.9)^{0.2t}&<\frac{1}{-30\ln(0.9)}\\\ln(0.9)^{0.2t}&<\ln\left(\frac{1}{-30\ln(0.9)}\right)\\0.2t&>\frac{\ln\left(\frac{1}{-30\ln(0.9)}\right)}{\ln(0.9)}\\0.2t&>10.9227\\t&>54.6\\t&>55\text{ min (nearest min)}\end{aligned}$$

Ian must wait 55 minutes.

For rest $\dot{x}=0$

$$\therefore\ -6e^{-2t}-e^{-t}+1=0$$

$\times e^{2t}$: $$\begin{aligned}-6-e^t+e^{2t}&=0\\(e^t)^2-e^t-6&=0\\(e^t+2)(e^t-3)&=0\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore\ e^t+2=0\quad$ or $\quad e^t-3=0$

$e^t=-2\qquad\qquad e^t=3$

no sol$^{\text{n}}\qquad\quad t=\ln3$

$\therefore$ at rest after $t=\ln3$ sec.
